_comment: Retired content URLs and where their intent now lives.
THIS FILE IS THE COMPLETE SET. scripts/generate-blog.js writes vercel.json's
`redirects` array from it wholesale — nothing is merged and nothing is
preserved from the previous file. That is deliberate: an earlier version
merged generated rules into whatever vercel.json already held, which meant
deleting an entry here left the old rule in place forever. Restoring a
retired page would then put it in the sitemap while Vercel kept redirecting
visitors away from it, and assertNoRetiredCollisions could not see the
problem because it reads this file rather than vercel.json.
So: to bring a page back, delete its entry here and the redirect goes with it.
Every entry is a permanent 301 to the closest SEMANTIC replacement — never a
blanket sweep into /blog/. A reader who searched for 'mining claims map
Nevada' and lands on the blog index has been given a 404 with a nicer
`patterns` are Vercel path-to-regexp sources, used where one rule retires a
whole generated family. `exact` handles individual pages. Order is preserved:
Vercel matches first-wins, so the specific jurisdiction entries in `exact`

patterns._note: 28 geographic permutations of one drill template. Every one of them targeted the same job — plot collars, label intercepts, export a figure — with the region name swapped. That job is one guide.

Catch-all for the 21 mining-claims-map regions where Exploration Maps has no jurisdiction-specific claim functionality: US states, Alberta, Nova Scotia, NWT, Western Australia, Chile, Peru, Mexico, South Africa, Ghana. The seven supported jurisdictions are listed in `exact` above and match first.
